one_liner: C# source-generated binary serializer that copies unmanaged data raw; ~1.7x faster than MessagePack-CSharp on objects, 40x+ on struct arrays.
what_it_does: MemoryPack is a .NET/Unity binary serializer for plain C# classes, structs and records. You mark a type [MemoryPackable] and partial, and a Roslyn source generator writes its formatter at compile time. The API has the same shape as MessagePack-CSharp: MemoryPackSerializer.Serialize writes to byte[], IBufferWriter<byte> or Stream, and Deserialize reads from ReadOnlySpan<byte>, ReadOnlySequence<byte> or Stream. There is also a ref overload that overwrites an existing instance. The wire format is its own and is not compatible with MessagePack or Protobuf.
how_it_is_fast: The format uses 'zero encoding'. It writes no field names or tags, members go in declaration order, ints are fixed-width little-endian (no varint), and the object header is a single member-count byte. Unmanaged structs and arrays of them are written with Unsafe.WriteUnaligned or one Unsafe.CopyBlockUnaligned (a memcpy) after a 4-byte length, which is why struct arrays are so much faster. Formatters are generated at compile time by the source generator (IMemoryPackable<T> with C# 11 static abstract members on net7.0+), with no reflection or IL.Emit. The writer is a ref struct that holds a `ref byte` into the destination span. The byte[] path reuses a [ThreadStatic] pinned ReusableLinkedArrayBufferWriter and allocates the result with GC.AllocateUninitializedArray. An optional UTF-16 string mode copies chars directly with no transcoding.
when_to_use: .NET-to-.NET traffic where both ends compile the same C# types: MagicOnion RPC, Redis/cache values, ASP.NET Core bodies through MemoryPack.AspNetCoreMvcFormatter, or local save files.
Payloads dominated by blittable structs or large unmanaged arrays (Vector3[], matrices, numeric buffers, game state), where serialization becomes a memcpy.
Unity 2022.3.12f1+ projects, including IL2CPP, that need reflection-free serialization. The README reports 3-10x faster than JsonUtility.
Allocation-sensitive hot paths that write straight into PipeWriter/IBufferWriter<byte>, or that reuse objects and lists through Deserialize(ref value).
C# servers talking to browser clients, using the generated TypeScript serializer instead of JSON.
when_not_to_use: Cross-language or public interchange (other than the generated TypeScript). The format is not self-describing, decoding needs the C# type, and there is no IDL, so use Protobuf or MessagePack there.

Size-sensitive payloads full of small integers. Ints are always 4 bytes, against 1-5 bytes with varint in MessagePack or Protobuf, so MemoryPack payloads can be larger. The README suggests LZ4/Zstd/Brotli compression.

Schemas that must evolve freely. The default mode allows only appending members: no deletes, reorders or type changes. Full version tolerance needs GenerateType.VersionTolerant, which the README says serializes slower and gives slightly larger payloads.
Big-endian targets. The reference implementation assumes little-endian and does not byte-swap.
Native AOT deployments. Issues #382 and #414 report 'Failed to create generic virtual method implementation' crashes, and both were closed by the stale bot without a fix in MemoryPack.

integration.form: shared lib (NuGet: MemoryPack = MemoryPack.Core runtime + MemoryPack.Generator Roslyn source generator; optional MemoryPack.Streaming, MemoryPack.AspNetCoreMvcFormatter, MemoryPack.UnityShims; Unity via NuGetForUnity plus a git-URL package)
integration.dependencies: none on net7.0/net8.0; the netstandard2.1 target pulls System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe 6.0.0 and System.Collections.Immutable 6.0.0
integration.min_toolchain: .NET Standard 2.1 (.NET 5/6) minimum, .NET 7+ recommended (targets net7.0, net8.0, netstandard2.1); Roslyn 4.3.1+ (VS 2022 17.3 / .NET SDK 6.0.401); Unity 2022.3.12f1+
integration.platforms: little-endian only (x86-64, arm64); .NET, Unity (IL2CPP included); Native AOT has open-ended crash reports
integration.thread_safety: The static MemoryPackSerializer keeps per-thread buffers and state in [ThreadStatic] fields, so concurrent calls from different threads are the intended use. Open issue #458 reports a NullReferenceException on parallel Deserialize, caused by a race in MemoryPackFormatterProvider.Register: Check<T>.registered is set before Cache<T>.formatter.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same attribute-plus-static-Serialize/Deserialize shape as MessagePack-CSharp, but types must be declared partial with [MemoryPackable], the wire format is incompatible with MessagePack/Protobuf (stored data must be migrated), and non-C# consumers are lost

gotchas: Member declaration order is the wire format. Reordering, deleting or retyping a member in the default mode breaks old data, and nothing on the wire detects it. The README recommends checking the generator's serialization-info output in CI.

Unmanaged structs are dumped as raw memory, padding included, and cannot take custom formatters (#440). Types with StructLayout.Auto, such as DateTimeOffset and ValueTuple, are not binary-compatible between .NET 7+ and Unity.
The netstandard2.1 and net7.0 builds do not mix. A MemoryPackable type compiled for netstandard2.1 and used from net7.0 throws TypeLoadException, so libraries must multi-target both.
Some collection formatters write BCL private fields through Unsafe.As view types (List<T>, Stack<T>, BitArray). Open issue #460 flags this as fragile on future runtimes.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Nino and HyperSerializer both report beating MemoryPack in their own READMEs (Nino 2.44x/1.90x on SimpleClass; HyperSerializer 2.14x round-trip). Pick MemoryPack for its broader feature set (unions, version-tolerant and circular-reference modes, TypeScript generation, ASP.NET Core formatter, Unity shims) and larger user base. Pick Nerdbank.MessagePack or MessagePack-CSharp when you need MessagePack wire compatibility, and Bebop when you need a cross-language schema.
verified_claims_summary: The README chart was run with BenchmarkDotNet on .NET 7 and a Ryzen 9 5950X, serializing into a reused ArrayBufferWriter; build flags are not stated. On the 47-field nested JsonResponseModel, MemoryPack serializes/deserializes in 13,176/24,540 ns against 22,961/39,420 ns for MessagePack-CSharp (~1.7x/1.6x) and 73,028/51,640 ns for protobuf-net (~5.5x/2.1x). On the panel labelled Vector3[10000] it takes 231/316 ns against MessagePack's 9,887/26,335 ns (~43x/83x). The checked-in SerializerTestBase builds 1,000 Vector3 elements, not 10,000, and the current Program.cs job uses 1 warmup and 1 iteration.
status_note: MIT with 4,739 stars and a stable NuGet package. The last library release is 1.21.4 (Feb 2025), and every commit since (latest 2026-07-08) is CI/chore work, so treat it as maintenance mode. Bugs such as #458 remain open, and the Native AOT crash reports were closed as stale without a fix.
